children: Italy said on Saturday it fully supported Germany's participation in the Global Combat Air Programme to develop a next-generation fighter jet, rejecting media reports that Rome had sought to block Berlin from joining.
The government said in a statement that a Financial Times report suggesting it had opposed Germany's entry was "entirely misleading" and did not reflect Rome's longstanding position.

Italy said it had always been willing to welcome Germany into GCAP and had proposed that Berlin initially join on an observer-only basis to facilitate information-sharing and speed its path towards full membership.
Rome said the proposal was designed to accelerate Germany's involvement while protecting the programme's timetable and progress, and was not intended to restrict Berlin's future role.

Italy reiterated its position during the latest GCAP videoconference involving the programme's three partner nations, it said in the statement, adding that it viewed German participation as "a positive opportunity".
